newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Zurich plans authorised, but no cap rise.
newsitem.headline: Zurich plans authorised, but no cap rise.

text.p: Zurich Group said it planned to create both authorised and contingent capital, but at this time it had no specific plans to increase its share capital.
The group will ask shareholders on June 11 to approve the creation of authorised capital of no more than 25 million Swiss francs, corresponding to a maximum of 2.5 million new shares.
It will also propose the creation of contingent capital of 35 million francs, or 3.5 million shares, of which one million shares will be reserved for employee share ownership plans.

"Acceptance of this proposal would give Zurich the necessary flexibility to issue additional shares or raise equity, which, for example, could be an important factor in the further expansion of our organisation," chairman Rolf Hueppi said in speech prepared for a news conference.
He also said the group did not plan to increase its share capital at this time.

"Financing the group's further expansion does not necessarily need to rely on additional share capital. There may be other opportunities to raise funds, e.g. through long-term borrowing -- keeping in mind acceptable debt/equity ratios and efficient structuring of such capital transactions," he said.
At the end of 1996 Zurich Group's share capital comprised 485.0 million francs.
